nodes.label: Products
nodes.description: End-user and developer products built on those blocks: coding agents, general assistants and browser agents.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.description: Open JSON-RPC protocol for exposing tools, resources and prompts to agent hosts. Latest revision I knew was 2025-11-25 (async tasks, URL-mode elicitation), with a stateful initialize handshake; donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in Dec 2025.

nodes.label: MCP Registry
nodes.description: Official community registry of published MCP servers, with a metadata format that clients and sub-registries can mirror. It gives clients one place to discover servers instead of per-vendor directories.

nodes.label: MCP authorization (OAuth-based)
nodes.description: The part of the MCP spec that has remote servers act as OAuth resource servers, with protected-resource metadata and client registration so hosts can obtain scoped tokens. It reuses OAuth 2.x and OpenID Connect discovery rather than inventing a new scheme.

nodes.label: Agent2Agent (A2A)
nodes.description: Google-originated agent-to-agent protocol (Agent Cards, tasks, streaming), donated to the Linux Foundation in June 2025. Latest I knew was v0.3 (gRPC, signed cards) from mid-2025.

nodes.label: Agent Communication Protocol (IBM/BeeAI)
nodes.description: REST-style agent messaging protocol from IBM's BeeAI that merged into A2A under the Linux Foundation in 2025. Kept as a node because the name is easy to confuse with the two other ACPs.

nodes.label: Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
nodes.description: Zed-created protocol for connecting coding agents to editors over JSON-RPC/stdio; JetBrains announced support in late 2025. Different from IBM's ACP and from the commerce ACP.

nodes.label: AG-UI
nodes.description: Event-based protocol between an agent backend and a user-facing app (web, mobile, chat), born from CopilotKit's work with LangChain and CrewAI. It streams messages, tool calls and state so a UI can render any compliant agent runtime.

nodes.label: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
nodes.description: Google's Agent Payments Protocol (Sept 2025): signed mandates for intent, cart and payment; extensible to stablecoins via x402.

nodes.label: Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)
nodes.description: Stripe and OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol (Sept 2025), behind Instant Checkout in ChatGPT, with Shared Payment Tokens.

nodes.label: x402
nodes.description: HTTP 402-based payment protocol, driven by Coinbase, that lets an agent pay for an API call with stablecoins in the request itself. AP2 lists it as one of its settlement extensions.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md
nodes.description: Plain Markdown file at a repo root that gives any coding agent project instructions (build, test, conventions). Contributed by OpenAI as a founding project of the Agentic AI Foundation, and read by Codex, Cursor, Amp, Factory, Kiro and many others.

nodes.label: Agent Skills (SKILL.md)
nodes.description: Anthropic's skills format (SKILL.md folders loaded on demand) published as an open standard in Dec 2025; adopted by a few other tools.

nodes.label: llms.txt
nodes.description: Convention for a Markdown index at a site's root that points models and agents at the most useful docs. MCP, agentskills.io and many doc sites now publish one.

nodes.label: Function / tool calling
nodes.description: The JSON-schema tool-call pattern that model APIs expose: the model emits a structured call, the host runs it and returns the result. MCP standardizes the layer above it, which servers define the tools.

nodes.label: OpenAI Responses API
nodes.description: OpenAI's agent-oriented API with built-in tools, state and conversations, replacing Chat Completions for new work and the Assistants API. The OpenAI Agents SDK is built on it.

nodes.label: Chat Completions API
nodes.description: The de facto messages-in, message-out API shape that most other providers and local servers imitate for compatibility.

nodes.label: OpenAI Assistants API
nodes.description: OpenAI's stateful assistant API (threads, runs, retrieval); deprecated in 2025 with a sunset planned for 2026.

nodes.label: Anthropic Messages API
nodes.description: Anthropic's API for Claude with tool use, extended thinking and prompt caching; the Claude Agent SDK and Claude Code call it.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions
nodes.description: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for LLM and agent spans, incubating inside the main semconv repo.

nodes.label: Linux Foundation
nodes.description: Neutral home for several agent standards. It hosts the Agentic AI Foundation and, separately, the A2A project.

nodes.label: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
nodes.description: Linux Foundation fund launched Dec 2025 by Anthropic, OpenAI and Block; founding projects MCP, goose, AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: LangGraph
nodes.description: Graph-based runtime for stateful, long-running agents with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop; v1.0 shipped in October 2025. LangChain 1.0 agents run on it.

nodes.label: LangChain
nodes.description: Original LLM application toolkit; agents via the older AgentExecutor, with LangGraph as the separate agent runtime.

nodes.label: CrewAI
nodes.description: Role-based multi-agent framework (crews and flows) written in Python and independent of LangChain.

nodes.label: LlamaIndex
nodes.description: Data and retrieval framework with an agent workflows layer, strongest for document-heavy agents.

nodes.label: OpenAI Agents SDK
nodes.description: OpenAI's SDK for agents, handoffs, guardrails and tracing on the Responses API (released March 2025); supports MCP tools.

nodes.label: Claude Agent SDK
nodes.description: Anthropic's SDK (Python, TypeScript) exposing the Claude Code agent loop, tools, hooks, subagents and MCP for custom agents. It was formerly called the Claude Code SDK.

nodes.label: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
nodes.description: Google's open-source agent framework, launched April 2025, with Python, Java, Go and TypeScript SDKs; it speaks A2A and MCP and deploys to Vertex AI Agent Engine.

nodes.label: AutoGen
nodes.description: Microsoft Research multi-agent conversation framework (v0.4 rewrite); AG2 is a community fork. Considered actively developed.

nodes.label: Semantic Kernel
nodes.description: Microsoft's SDK for plugins, planners and agents in .NET, Python and Java; Microsoft's main enterprise agent SDK.

nodes.label: Strands Agents
nodes.description: AWS's open-source model-driven agent SDK, the framework behind many Bedrock AgentCore examples.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.description: TypeScript-first agent and workflow framework with memory, evals and MCP support.

nodes.label: Pydantic AI
nodes.description: Type-safe Python agent framework from the Pydantic team, with MCP and A2A support.

nodes.label: smolagents
nodes.description: Hugging Face's minimal library where agents write actions as code.

nodes.label: Vercel AI SDK
nodes.description: TypeScript toolkit for streaming UI, tools and agent loops across model providers.

nodes.label: Haystack
nodes.description: deepset's pipeline framework for retrieval and agent applications.

nodes.label: OpenHands
nodes.description: Open-source software-agent platform and SDK (formerly OpenDevin) usable both as a product and as a library for building coding agents.

nodes.label: Mem0
nodes.description: Memory layer with Python and Node SDKs, an MCP integration and OpenMemory; its site currently emphasizes benchmarks on LoCoMo, LongMemEval and BEAM.

nodes.label: Letta
nodes.description: Stateful-agent platform that grew out of the MemGPT research project at UC Berkeley, with self-editing memory blocks.

nodes.label: Zep
nodes.description: Context and memory service built on a temporal knowledge graph; its open-source engine is Graphiti.

nodes.label: Graphiti
nodes.description: Open-source temporal knowledge-graph library for agent memory, maintained by Zep.

nodes.label: Cognee
nodes.description: Open-source memory engine that builds graph and vector memory from documents and interactions.

nodes.label: LangMem
nodes.description: LangChain's memory SDK for LangGraph agents (extraction and prompt refinement).

nodes.label: Claude memory tool & CLAUDE.md
nodes.description: File-based memory for Claude: a memory tool in the API plus CLAUDE.md project and user instructions that Claude Code loads every session.

nodes.label: E2B
nodes.description: Firecracker-microVM sandboxes for running agent-generated code; one of the providers the OpenAI Agents SDK supports natively.

nodes.label: Daytona
nodes.description: Fast-starting sandbox infrastructure for agents; supported by the OpenAI Agents SDK.

nodes.label: Modal
nodes.description: Serverless compute with sandboxes and GPUs, popular for Python-heavy agent workloads.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Sandboxes & Agents
nodes.description: TypeScript-first sandboxes and the Agents SDK on Workers, with remote MCP server hosting.

nodes.label: Vercel Sandbox
nodes.description: Ephemeral microVMs for running untrusted agent code from Vercel apps.

nodes.label: Composio
nodes.description: Managed tool and integration layer that exposes hundreds of SaaS apps to agents with auth handled for you, via SDK or MCP.

nodes.label: Browserbase
nodes.description: Hosted headless browsers for agents, the backend behind Stagehand.

nodes.label: Stagehand
nodes.description: Browserbase's open-source SDK that mixes Playwright code with natural-language browser actions.

nodes.label: Browser Use
nodes.description: Open-source Python library that lets an LLM drive a browser; widely used to build custom web agents.

nodes.label: Playwright MCP
nodes.description: Microsoft's MCP server that gives agents browser control through accessibility snapshots.

nodes.label: goose
nodes.description: Block's open-source local agent and an AAIF founding project; extensible through MCP servers.

nodes.label: OpenAI AgentKit
nodes.description: OpenAI's visual agent builder, ChatKit and evals bundle announced in October 2025, running on the Responses API.

nodes.label: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
nodes.description: AWS managed runtime, memory, gateway and identity services for deploying agents from any framework.

nodes.label: Vertex AI Agent Engine
nodes.description: Google Cloud's managed runtime for ADK and other agents, with A2A support.

nodes.label: Microsoft Copilot Studio / Foundry Agent Service
nodes.description: Microsoft's low-code and pro-code hosting for agents, with MCP and A2A support.

nodes.label: SWE-bench Verified
nodes.description: The headline coding-agent benchmark: 500 human-validated GitHub issues scored by hidden tests.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench
nodes.description: Stanford/Laude terminal-task benchmark for agents (v1 launched May 2025).

nodes.label: OSWorld
nodes.description: Benchmark of computer-use agents completing tasks in real desktop apps from screenshots; integrity problems have led to curated subsets.

nodes.label: WebArena
nodes.description: Self-hostable web environments for testing browser agents on realistic site tasks.

nodes.label: tau-bench
nodes.description: Sierra's benchmark of tool-using agents in simulated customer-service domains with policies.

nodes.label: GAIA
nodes.description: General AI assistant benchmark of questions that need browsing, tools and reasoning.

nodes.label: Inspect
nodes.description: UK AI Security Institute's open-source framework for writing and running model and agent evals.

nodes.label: Braintrust
nodes.description: Evaluation and logging platform for LLM apps and agents.

nodes.label: LangSmith
nodes.description: LangChain's tracing, evaluation and deployment platform.

nodes.label: Langfuse
nodes.description: Open-source LLM observability and prompt management, OpenTelemetry-friendly.

nodes.label: Arize Phoenix
nodes.description: Open-source tracing and evaluation built on OpenInference and OpenTelemetry.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.description: Anthropic's terminal-first coding agent (plus IDE, desktop and web) with subagents, hooks, plugins, skills and MCP. Reviewers in 2026 roundups rank it at or near the top for deep reasoning, debugging and large refactors.

nodes.label: OpenAI Codex
nodes.description: OpenAI's coding agent across CLI, IDE, cloud and app, bundled with ChatGPT plans; it reads AGENTS.md and speaks MCP, and is available in editors through ACP. Roundups place it alongside Claude Code at the top, valued for cost.

nodes.label: Cursor
nodes.description: AI-native editor (VS Code fork) with agent mode and background agents; rated the strongest daily IDE experience in 2026 comparisons, and now also usable inside JetBrains IDEs via ACP.

nodes.label: GitHub Copilot
nodes.description: Microsoft/GitHub's assistant with agent mode in VS Code and JetBrains and a cloud coding agent that works on issues and opens PRs; the default fit for GitHub-centered organizations.

nodes.label: Devin
nodes.description: Cognition's autonomous software engineer that takes whole tickets in a cloud workspace.

nodes.label: Windsurf
nodes.description: Windsurf, the agentic IDE (Cascade agent), acquired by Cognition in mid-2025 after OpenAI's deal fell through.

nodes.label: Gemini CLI
nodes.description: Google's open-source terminal agent with MCP support and a generous free tier; one 2026 roundup names it the best free option.

nodes.label: Jules
nodes.description: Google's asynchronous cloud coding agent that works on GitHub repos and returns PRs.

nodes.label: Kiro
nodes.description: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE (requirements, design, tasks), launched in preview July 2025.

nodes.label: Amp
nodes.description: Sourcegraph's agentic coding tool for terminal and editor; contributed to AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Cline
nodes.description: Open-source VS Code coding agent with human-approval steps and MCP marketplace.

nodes.label: Roo Code
nodes.description: Open-source VS Code agent forked from Cline, with custom modes.

nodes.label: OpenCode
nodes.description: Open-source terminal coding agent that works with many model providers.

nodes.label: Aider
nodes.description: Long-running open-source terminal pair-programmer with git-native edits.

nodes.label: goose (app)
nodes.description: Block's local agent app and CLI, built from the goose framework.

nodes.label: OpenHands (product)
nodes.description: Open-source cloud and local coding agent from All Hands AI.

nodes.label: Zed
nodes.description: High-performance editor with built-in agent panel and the origin of ACP.

nodes.label: JetBrains Junie
nodes.description: JetBrains' coding agent, with its IDEs also hosting third-party agents through ACP.

nodes.label: Factory Droids
nodes.description: Enterprise agent platform ('Droids') for software delivery; one of the AGENTS.md co-developers.

nodes.label: Replit Agent
nodes.description: Browser-based agent that builds and deploys apps in Replit's environment.

nodes.label: Lovable
nodes.description: Prompt-to-app builder aimed at non-developers; similar tools include Bolt and v0.

nodes.label: v0
nodes.description: Vercel's prompt-to-UI and app generator.

nodes.label: Warp
nodes.description: Agentic terminal with built-in coding agents.

nodes.label: Claude (apps) & Cowork
nodes.description: Claude apps with Projects, connectors, skills and computer-use features; no dedicated desktop work agent that I knew of.

nodes.label: ChatGPT (agent mode)
nodes.description: OpenAI's assistant with agent mode (Operator merged in mid-2025), Atlas as its dedicated browser, and apps via the Apps SDK.

nodes.label: Gemini (Agent)
nodes.description: Google's assistant, with Gemini Agent absorbing the Project Mariner technology.

nodes.label: OpenClaw
nodes.description: Viral open-source personal agent (Nov 2025) that went through several names; maintained by Peter Steinberger.

nodes.label: Manus
nodes.description: General-purpose cloud agent that plans and executes multi-step tasks; I could not verify its current ownership in this research.

nodes.label: Microsoft 365 Copilot
nodes.description: Microsoft's work assistant with agents built in Copilot Studio.

nodes.label: ChatGPT Atlas
nodes.description: OpenAI's Chromium-based AI browser for macOS (Oct 2025) with an agent mode; active product.

nodes.label: Perplexity Comet
nodes.description: Perplexity's agentic browser, now free with a paid Max tier and available on Android; a federal court blocked its agent from Amazon's logged-in pages in March 2026.

nodes.label: Claude in Chrome
nodes.description: Anthropic's Chrome extension for browser tasks, in limited research preview (Aug 2025).

nodes.label: Gemini in Chrome (Auto Browse)
nodes.description: Chrome's built-in Gemini assistant; Auto Browse launched on 28 January 2026 and runs multi-step tasks for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

nodes.label: Project Mariner
nodes.description: Google DeepMind's experimental browser agent, available to AI Ultra subscribers.

nodes.label: OpenAI Operator
nodes.description: OpenAI's first browser agent (January 2025); merged into ChatGPT agent mode in mid-2025.

nodes.label: Salesforce Agentforce
nodes.description: Salesforce's platform for business agents; Salesforce sits on the A2A technical steering committee.

nodes.label: ServiceNow AI Agents
nodes.description: ServiceNow's workflow agents; ServiceNow is on the A2A steering committee.

nodes.label: SAP Joule agents
nodes.description: SAP's assistant and agents; SAP is on the A2A steering committee.
